newsitem.title: USA: Whitacre no longer cooperating with U.S. government.
newsitem.headline: Whitacre no longer cooperating with U.S. government.

text.p: Former Archer Daniels Midland Co. executive Mark Whitacre, who acted as an informant for three years in a U.S. Justice Department price-fixing probe, said Tuesday he was no longer cooperating with the U.S. government.
Whitacre, who was indicted Tuesday along with two other former ADM officials, said, "I have decided not to participate in the government's coverup any longer." He did not elaborate.

Asked to comment on the indictment against him, Whitacre said, "I have no comment other than when all the evidence comes out in this case, the only people that will have questions yet to answer will be the Justice Department and the FBI itself."

Earlier today, the Justice Department said a federal grand jury in Chicago indicted Whitacre, along with Michael Andreas, the former ADM executive vice president and vice chairman, and Terrance Wilson, a former group vice president. Michael Andreas is the son of ADM Chairman Dwayne Andreas.

Whitacre was fired by ADM in August 1995 on charges he allegedly stole $9 million from the company. Whitacre has denied the charges and recently filed a wrongful dismissal suit against the Decatur, Ill.-based agricultural products giant.
ADM in October pleaded guilty to two counts of fixing prices for the food additives lysine and citric acid and agreed to pay $100 million in fines.
